The present appeal has been preferred for setting aside the award dated 28.08.2017 passed in the claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sangrur (for short, 'the Tribunal'), whereby, claim petition filed by the appellant/claimant, was allowed and appellant-insurance company was held liable to pay the National Insurance Company Ltd vs Hardev Kaur And Ors on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49949182/

sentences.text:
The award is challenged on the ground that no contributory negligence was attributed on the deceased (Husandeep Singh) as well as quantum of compensation being on higher side.
1 of 16 FACTS NOT IN DISPUTE 2.

Brief facts of the case is that on 16.10.2016 at about 10:30 pm, the deceased alongwith Sandeep Singh son of Major Singh, resident of Mohan Nagar, Bhawanigarh and Pargat Singh son of Hardev Singh was coming from village Ghabadan towards Bhawanigarh on his motorcycle bearing registration No.PB-13AH-8573 make TVS Sport after doing his job.
Husandeep Singh was the main rider whereas Sandeep Singh and Pargat Singh were pillion riders on the aforesaid motorcycle.
When they reached at Main Road, Bhawanigarh near Beas Ghar then the driver of Truck/Trolla bearing registration No.RJ-07GA- 4230 suddenly took a sharp cut.

Husandeep Singh deceased applied breaks of the motorcycle,
however his motorcycle struck into the Trolla at its rear.
side, due to which Sandeep Singh, Pargat Singh and Husandeep Singh suffered injuries.

Hussandeep Singh's head struck with the rear portion of Truck/Trolla, due to which he suffered head injury and as a result of which, he died on the spot and his motorcycle bearing registration No.PB-13AH-8573 was also badly damaged.
It is alleged that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1.
In this regard, the FIR was got lodged by Sandeep Singh son of Major Singh, against respondent No.1.
It is further averred that said accident was witnessed by Sandeep Singh son of Major Singh and Pargat Singh and other passersby.

Regarding the occupation and of deceased, it is averred that deceased was the age of 20 years and he was working as skilled labourer at I.A.L. Factory, Ghabdan and besides this, he was helping his father in the business of buffaloes and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

The claimants No.1 to 3 were dependent upon the income of deceased and he was sole bread winner of the family and due to the untimely death of the 2 of 16 deceased, the claimants have been deprived of the love and affection.
It is averred that claimants spent Rs.50,000/- on the funeral and last rites of the deceased.
3. Upon notice of the claim petition, the respondents appeared and filed their separate replies denying the factum of accident/compensation.

4. From the pleadings of the parties, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues:-
"1.

Whether Husandeep Singh died in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 16.10.2016 on account ofrash and negligent driving of Trolla bearing registration No.RJ-07GA-4230 which was being driven by respondent No.1?
OPP 2.
If issue No.1 is proved, whether the claimants are entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from
whom?OPR 3.
Whether the respondent No.1 was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident, if so its effect?

sentences.text:
After taking into consideration the pleadings and the evidence on record, the learned Tribunal allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation to the claimant to the tune of Rs.16,07,312/-
and the appellant-Insurance Company was held liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, the present appeal.
3 of 16 SUBMISSIONS OF LEARNED COUNSEL FOR THE PARTIES 6.

Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company contends that the learned Tribunal has committed a manifest error in holding that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the tralla bearing registration No. RJ-07-GA-4230 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) by its driver, Jagdish Singh (hereinafter referred to as the driver of the offending vehicle).
He further submits that the said finding is contrary to the evidence available on record and suffers from non- application of mind.

He further contends that the deceased himself was guilty of contributory negligence, inasmuch as he was riding the motorcycle with two pillion riders in violation of statutory provisions and traffic norms.
Such conduct on the part of the deceased materially contributed to the occurrence of the accident.
Therefore, the learned Tribunal erred in not attributing contributory negligence to the deceased, and the present case ought to have been adjudicated as one involving contributory negligence.
Learned counsel further submits that the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is excessive and disproportionate to the facts and circumstances of the case.
He contends that the Tribunal has erroneously added 50% of the income towards future prospects, whereas as per the settled position of law, only 40% addition was permissible.

He also contends that the learned Tribunal has wrongly deducted one-third (1/3rd) of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, whereas in view of the number of dependents and 4 of 16 the settled legal principles, deduction of one-half (1/2) ought to have been made.

Additionally, he argues that the amount awarded under the conventional heads, such as loss of consortium and funeral expenses, is also on the higher side and not in conformity with the parameters laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
On the aforesaid grounds, learned counsel for the appellant prays that the present appeal be allowed, the impugned award be suitably modified, and the compensation be reduced accordingly.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondents, however, vehemently argues on the lines of the award dated 28.08.2017.
Therefore, they pray for dismissal of the appeal.

He further deposed that he alongwith deceased was coming from village Ghabdan towards Bhawanigarh on motorcycle bearing registration No.PB-13AH- 8573 make TVS Sport after doing the job.

He further deposed that head of Husandeep Singh struck with the rear side of the Trolla and due to the head injury, he died on the spot and the motorcycle bearing registration No.PB-13AH- 8573 was also badly damaged.

sentences.text: 13. In the present case, CW-2 Sandeep Singh (eye witness) has proved the manner of the accident and he remained consistent in deposing the rash and negligent act of respondent No.1 in driving the vehicle.
The postmortem report has clearly established that deceased died due to the injuries received in the accident.

The witness stood the test of cross examination and it has been proved on the case file that accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 and consequently deceased Husandeep Singh died on account of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.

He further argued that the driving license of the deceased Husandeep Singh has not been produced by claimants.

sentences.text:
Hon'ble High Court has laid down the criteria for addition of future prospects in case of labouer as under.
"24.
A labourer who received a daily wages of Rs.50/- about seven years ago has started getting at least a sum of Rs.150-200/- per day.
Though, there is no fixed increment for him on his daily wages, the minimum wages periodically increased by the Stated government concerned taking into account the cost of living.
In fact, the cost of living affects one and all, irrespective of the class to which the victim belong.
A labourer who gets a sum of Rs.3750/- per month would not be getting the same wages even after 70 long years.

In view of the above, I find that applying the principle of 30% additions towards the future prospects of the deceased who was a labourer without considering the slap contemplated in the case of Sarla Verma (supra) would be unfair, inappropriate and discriminatory.

In view of above, I find that 50 % of the income in case of a labourer of wage or a person with a fixed salary without increment in case he was below 40 years and 30% income in case he was 11 of 16 between 40-50 years will have to be added towards their future prospects while calculating loss of dependency."

25. Applying the ratio of authoritative pronouncement of Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana, the claimants are entitled for addition of 50% of income of deceased under the head of future prospects as deceased was less than 40 years of age at the time of death.

A perusal of the impugned award reveals that the learned Tribunal has rightly held that the accident in question occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

11. The record demonstrates that the eye-witness to the accident, CW-2 Sandeep Singh, gave a clear,
cogent, and consistent account of the entire sequence of events leading to the accident.
CW-2 Sandeep Singh categorically attributed rashness and negligence to the driver of the offending vehicle.

It is significant to note that the FIR (Ex. C-11) was lodged promptly after the occurrence of the accident by the said eye-witness, and the version recorded therein is in complete consonance with his deposition before the learned Tribunal.
This consistency lends substantial credibility to his testimony.
CW-2 (Eye witness) withstood the test of cross-examination, and no material contradiction or infirmity could be elicited so as to discredit his version.

His testimony, therefore,
remained unimpeached and trustworthy.

12. It further transpires from the record that the appellant-Insurance Company did not raise any specific plea of contributory negligence in the written statement filed by them before the learned Tribunal.

In the absence of such a plea, no issue regarding contributory negligence was framed by National Insurance Company Ltd vs Hardev Kaur And Ors on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49949182/
8 the learned Tribunal.

sentences.text: Moreover, no evidence whatsoever was led by the appellant-Insurance Company to establish that the deceased Husandeep Singh had contributed to the occurrence of the accident.
Even during the cross-examination of CW-2 Sandeep Singh, no suggestion was put to him alleging contributory negligence on the part of the deceased in driving the motorcycle.

This Court is constrained to reiterate that the principle of contributory negligence requires a specific and conscious inquiry into the conduct of the injured person or the deceased, and a clear finding as to how such conduct contributed to the occurrence of the accident.

14. Contributory negligence cannot be presumed or inferred merely on the basis of an alleged violation of traffic rules, unless it is established by cogent and reliable evidence that such violation materially contributed to the accident.

15. Even assuming that the deceased was riding the motorcycle with two pillion riders, the burden squarely lay upon the appellant-Insurance Company to demonstrate that such act had a direct nexus with the occurrence of the accident.
In the absence of any such evidence, no finding of contributory negligence can be sustained.
16. From the foregoing discussion, it is evident that the appellant- Insurance Company failed to adduce any evidence to substantiate the plea of contributory negligence.
Consequently, the learned Tribunal was fully justified in concluding that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
The findings recorded by the learned Tribunal on this issue, therefore, call for no interference and are hereby affirmed.
17. Coming to the question of quantum, it is not in dispute that the deceased was about 20 years of age and was engaged as a labourer at the time of the accident.
18. The learned Tribunal has added 50% of the income towards future prospects.

However, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble 14 of 16 Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, [(2017) 16 SCC 680] the addition towards future prospects in the case of a deceased below the age of 40 years and engaged in any other employment than a government employment ought to be 40%.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition of 50% is, therefore, unsustainable and is reduced to 40%.
19. It is further evident from the record that the deceased was unmarried.

As per the settled ratio in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another [(2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121],
where the deceased is a bachelor, the appropriate deduction towards personal and living expenses is one-half (1/2) of the income.

sentences.text: The learned Tribunal, however, deducted only one-third (1/3rd), which is contrary to settled law.

The deduction is accordingly modified to one-half (1/2).

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
11. Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana in case titled as Girdhari Lal Vs. Radhe Shyam and other 1993 (2) PLR 109 has observed that when the driver was facing criminal trial, it has to 6 of 16 be prima-facie concluded that the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.
13. In the present case, CW-2 Sandeep Singh (eye witness) has proved the manner of the accident and he remained consistent in deposing the rash and negligent act of respondent No.1 in driving the vehicle.
The postmortem report has clearly established that deceased died due to the injuries received in the accident.
The occurrence of accident with the offending vehicle has also been proved.
In the General Manager ICICI Lombard Vs. Rajinder Singh and others 2016 AAC 2314, Hon'ble Karnataka High Court turned down the plea of the insurance company for contributing negligence of deceased driver on the ground that insurer in its written statement did not advance the plea of contributory negligence on the part of driver of the bus, the MACT did not frame any issue or point for consideration over contributing negligence and oral testimony of witnesses for the insurer did not testify to contribution of negligence of the driver of the bus.
In view of absence of aforesaid plea, in the pleadings, no issue in this regard was framed.
No evidence has been led by the insurance company to prove the contributory negligence of deceased Husandeep Singh.
Moreover,
in the cross examination of Sandeep Singh (eye witness) no suggestion has been given to the witness regarding the contributory negligence of deceased Husandeep Singh in driving the motorcycle.
The respondents have not put any question to the claimants' witnesses regarding the age of the deceased.
It shows that age of the deceased has been admitted by the respondents and they have not disputed the aforesaid fact.
Accordingly, this Tribunal holds that deceased was of the age of 20 years at the time of death.
26. No amount of money can compensate the loss of a human life.
No amount of money can wipe the tears, the trauma of the claimants.
Therefore, the claimants are also entitled to get non pecuniary compensation towards loss of love, affection, loss to estate and the National Insurance Company Ltd vs Hardev Kaur And Ors on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49949182/
7
It is significant to note that the FIR (Ex. C-11) was lodged promptly after the occurrence of the accident by the said eye-witness, and the version recorded therein is in complete consonance with his deposition before the learned Tribunal.
CW-2 (Eye witness) withstood the test of cross-examination, and no material contradiction or infirmity could be elicited so as to discredit his version.
His testimony, therefore,
remained unimpeached and trustworthy.
This Court is constrained to reiterate that the principle of contributory negligence requires a specific and conscious inquiry into the conduct of the injured person or the deceased, and a clear finding as to how such conduct contributed to the occurrence of the accident.
14. Contributory negligence cannot be presumed or inferred merely on the basis of an alleged violation of traffic rules, unless it is established by cogent and reliable evidence that such violation materially contributed to the accident.
15. Even assuming that the deceased was riding the motorcycle with two pillion riders, the burden squarely lay upon the appellant-Insurance Company to demonstrate that such act had a direct nexus with the occurrence of the accident.
In the absence of any such evidence, no finding of contributory negligence can be sustained.
Consequently, the learned Tribunal was fully justified in concluding that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
However, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble 14 of 16 Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, [(2017) 16 SCC 680] the addition towards future prospects in the case of a deceased below the age of 40 years and engaged in any other employment than a government employment ought to be 40%.
As per the settled ratio in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another [(2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121],
where the deceased is a bachelor, the appropriate deduction towards personal and living expenses is one-half (1/2) of the income.
The learned Tribunal has rightly held that respondent No.4, the married brother of the deceased, was not financially dependent upon him.
However, the Tribunal failed to award filial consortium to respondent No.4, which is permissible in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
